Best way to use Image Resizer

Image Resizer is built for exact pixel-size tasks: form photos, profile images, website thumbnails, and social media images.

Best for

  • Changing photo width and height for online forms
  • Creating smaller website thumbnails
  • Keeping aspect ratio while resizing large phone photos

Example workflow

Example: upload a 4000px phone photo, set width to 1200px, keep aspect ratio, and download a smaller web-ready image.

Quality notes

Resizing before compression usually produces better quality than aggressive compression alone.

Before you download

  • Check that the output format matches the website, form, or software where you will upload it.
  • Open the downloaded file once before final submission so you can confirm quality, page order, dimensions, and readability.
  • If the result is too large, use the related compression or resize tools instead of repeating the same step many times.
  • If the source file is password-protected, corrupted, scanned, or extremely large, use a desktop or specialist tool when browser processing is not enough.

Troubleshooting

  • Use keep aspect ratio to avoid stretched faces or logos.
  • For strict file-size limits, resize first and then compress.
  • PNG is best for transparency; JPG/WebP are usually smaller for photos.

Common uses for Image Resizer

  • prepare photos for forms and profiles
  • optimize website images
  • convert images for compatibility

Tips for better results

For the best balance of size and quality, start with a clear original image and choose JPG or WebP for smaller photo files.
